SECTION 4. EFFECTIVE DATE 
SECTION 5. DRAFTING INFORMATION 
SECTION 1. PURPOSE 
     This revenue procedure sets forth inflation-adjusted items for 2027 for various Code 
provisions as in effect on [Release Date, 2026]. The inflation adjusted items for the 
Code sections set forth in section 3 of this revenue procedure are generally determined 
by reference to § 1(f). If amendments to the Code are enacted for 2027 after [Release 
Date, 2026], taxpayers should consult additional guidance to determine whether these 
adjustments remain applicable for 2027. 
SECTION 2. CHANGES 
     .01 Section 70431 of Public Law 119-21, 139 Stat. 72 (July 4, 2025), commonly 
known as the One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act amends § 1202(b). Certain amounts referred 
to in § 1202(b) are adjusted for inflation for years beginning after 2026. 
SECTION 3. 2027 ADJUSTED ITEMS

 .02 Unearned Income of Minor Children Subject to the "Kiddie Tax". For taxable 
years beginning in 2027, the amount in § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I), which is used to reduce the 
net unearned income reported on the child's return that is subject to the "kiddie tax," is 
$1,400. This $1,400 amount is the same as the amount provided in § 63(c)(5)(A), as 
adjusted for inflation. The same $1,400 amount is used for purposes of § 1(g)(7) to 
determine whether a parent may elect to include a child's gross income in the parent's 
gross income and to calculate the "kiddie tax." For example, one of the requirements for 
the parental election is that a child's gross income is more than the amount referred to 
in § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) but less than 10 times that amount; thus, a child's gross income for 
2027 must be more than $1,400 but less than $14,000. 
.03 Maximum Capital Gains Rate (§ 1(h), § 1(j)(5)). For taxable years beginning in 
2027, the maximum zero rate amounts and maximum 15 percent rate amounts under 
§ 1(j)(5)(B), as adjusted for inflation, are as follows: 
Filing Status Maximum Zero

  .04 Adoption Credit.
 (1) Adoption Credit for Children with Special Needs. For taxable years beginning in 
2027, under § 23(a)(3), the credit allowed for an adoption of a child with special needs 
is $18,250. 
(2) Adoption Credit Limitation. For taxable years beginning in 2027, under 
§ 23(b)(1), the maximum credit allowed for other adoptions is the amount of qualified 
adoption expenses up to $18,250. The available adoption credit begins to phase out 
under § 23(b)(2)(A) for taxpayers with modified adjusted gross income in excess of 
$273,680 and is completely phased out for taxpayers with modified adjusted gross 
income of $313,680 or more. See section 3.20 of this revenue procedure for the 
adjusted items relating to adoption assistance programs. 
(3) Refundable Portion. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the amount used in 
§ 23(a)(4) to determine the amount of the credit under § 23 that may be refundable is 
$5,280. 
.05 Child Tax Credit. 
(1) Maximum amount of the credit. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the 
maximum amount of the credit allowed under § 24(a) is $2,300. 
(2) Refundable portion. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the amount used in 
§ 24(d)(1)(A) to determine the amount of the credit under § 24 that may be refundable is 
$1,800. 
.06 Earned Income Credit. 
(1) In general. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the following amounts are 
used to determine the earned income credit under § 32(b). The "earned income 
amount" is the amount of earned income at or above which the maximum amount of the 
 
 
earned income credit is allowed. The "threshold phaseout amount" is the amount of 
adjusted gross income (or, if greater, earned income) above which the maximum 
amount of the credit begins to phase out. The "completed phaseout amount" is the 
amount of adjusted gross income (or, if greater, earned income) at or above which no 
credit is allowed. The threshold phaseout amounts and the completed phaseout 
amounts shown in the table below for married taxpayers filing a joint return include the 
increase provided in § 32(b)(2)(B), as adjusted for inflation for taxable years beginning 
in 2027. The threshold phaseout amounts and the completed phaseout amounts shown 
in the table below for taxpayers with all other filing statuses also apply to married 
taxpayers who are not filing a joint return and satisfy the special rules for separated 
spouses in § 32(d).

(2) Excessive Investment Income. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the earned 
income tax credit is not allowed under § 32(i) if the aggregate amount of certain 
investment income exceeds $12,600. 
.07 Rehabilitation Expenditures Treated as Separate New Building. For calendar 
year 2027, the per low-income unit qualified basis amount under § 42(e)(3)(A)(ii)(II) is 
$9,000. 
 
 
 
 
 
 .08 Low-Income Housing Credit. For calendar year 2027, the amount used under 
§ 42(h)(3)(C)(ii) to calculate the State housing credit ceiling for the low-income housing 
credit is the greater of (1) $3.53 multiplied by the State population, or (2) $4,082,400. 
.09 Employer-Provided Child Care Credit. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the 
maximum allowable credit under § 45F(b) is $515,943.67 ($619,132.40 in the case of 
an eligible small business). 
.10 Employee Health Insurance Expense of Small Employers. For taxable years 
beginning in 2027, the dollar amount in effect under § 45R(d)(3)(B) is $35,162.04. This 
amount is used under § 45R(c) for limiting the small employer health insurance credit 
and under § 45R(d)(1)(B) for determining who is an eligible small employer for purposes 
of the credit. 
.11 Exemption Amounts for Alternative Minimum Tax. For taxable years beginning in 
2027, the exemption amounts under § 55(d)(1) are: 
Joint Returns or Surviving Spouses $144,700

Estates and Trusts $32,500

.12 Alternative Minimum Tax Exemption for a Child Subject to the "Kiddie Tax." For 
taxable years beginning in 2027, for a child to whom the § 1(g) "kiddie tax" applies, the 
exemption amount under §§ 55(d) and 59(j) for purposes of the alternative minimum tax 
under § 55 may not exceed the sum of (1) the child's earned income for the taxable 
year, plus (2) $10,050. 
.13 Certain Expenses of Elementary and Secondary School Teachers. For taxable 
years beginning in 2027, under § 62(a)(2)(D), the amount of the deduction allowed 
under § 162 that consists of expenses paid or incurred by an eligible educator in 
connection with books, supplies (other than nonathletic supplies for courses of 
instruction in health or physical education), computer equipment (including related 
software and services) and other equipment, and supplementary materials used by the 
eligible educator in the classroom is $350. 
.14 Transportation Mainline Pipeline Construction Industry Optional Expense 
Substantiation Rules for Payments to Employees Under Accountable Plans. For 
calendar year 2027, an eligible employer may pay certain welders and heavy equipment 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
  
 
 
mechanics an amount up to $23 per hour for rig-related expenses that are deemed 
substantiated under an accountable plan if paid in accordance with Rev. Proc. 2002-41, 
2002-1 C.B. 1098. If the employer provides fuel or otherwise reimburses fuel expenses, 
an amount up to $14 per hour is deemed substantiated if paid in accordance with Rev. 
Proc. 2002-41. 
.15 Standard Deduction. 
(1) In general. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the standard deduction 
amounts under § 63(c)(2) are as follows: 
Filing Status Standard 
Deduction 
Married Individuals Filing Joint Returns and Surviving Spouses 
(§ 1(j)(2)(A)) 
$33,200  
Heads of Households (§ 1(j)(2)(B)) $24,925 
Unmarried Individuals (other than Surviving Spouses and Heads of 
Households) (§ 1(j)(2)(C)) 
$16,600  
Married Individuals Filing Separate Returns (§ 1(j)(2)(D)) $16,600 
(2) Dependent. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the standard deduction 
amount under § 63(c)(5) for an individual who may be claimed as a dependent by 
another taxpayer cannot exceed the greater of (1) $1,400, or (2) the sum of $500 and 
the individual's earned income. 
(3) Aged or blind. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the additional standard 
deduction amount under § 63(f) for the aged or the blind is $1,700. The additional 
standard deduction amount is increased to $2,100 if the individual is also unmarried and 
not a surviving spouse. 
 
 
 .16 Cafeteria Plans. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the dollar limitation under 
§ 125(i) on voluntary employee salary reductions for contributions to health flexible 
spending arrangements is $3,500. If the cafeteria plan permits the carryover of unused 
amounts, the maximum carryover amount is $700. 
.17 Educational Assistance Program Exclusion. For taxable years beginning in 2027, 
the amount that can be excluded from an employee's gross income under § 127(a) for 
educational assistance is $5,400. 
.18 Qualified Transportation Fringe Benefit. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the 
monthly limitation under § 132(f)(2)(A) regarding the aggregate fringe benefit exclusion 
amount for transportation in a commuter highway vehicle and any transit pass is $350. 
The monthly limitation under § 132(f)(2)(B) regarding the fringe benefit exclusion 
amount for qualified parking is $350. 
.19 Income from United States Savings Bonds for Taxpayers Who Pay Qualified 
Higher Education Expenses. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the exclusion under 
§ 135, regarding income from United States savings bonds for taxpayers who pay 
qualified higher education expenses, begins to phase out for modified adjusted gross 
income above $157,600 for joint returns and $105,100 for all other returns. The 
exclusion is completely phased out for modified adjusted gross income of $187,600 or 
more for joint returns and $120,100 or more for all other returns. 
.20 Adoption Assistance Programs. For taxable years beginning in 2027, under 
§ 137(a)(2), the amount that can be excluded from an employee's gross income for the 
adoption of a child with special needs is $18,250. For taxable years beginning in 2027, 
under § 137(b)(1) the maximum amount that can be excluded from an employee's gross 
 
 
 
income for the amounts paid or expenses incurred by an employer for qualified adoption 
expenses furnished pursuant to an adoption assistance program for adoptions by the 
employee is $18,250. The amount excludable from an employee's gross income begins 
to phase out under § 137(b)(2)(A) for taxpayers with modified adjusted gross income in 
excess of $273,680 and is completely phased out for taxpayers with modified adjusted 
gross income of $313,680 or more. See section 3.04 of this revenue procedure for the 
adjusted items relating to the adoption credit. 
.21 Private Activity Bonds Volume Cap. For calendar year 2027, the amounts used 
under § 146(d) to calculate the State ceiling for the volume cap for private activity bonds 
is the greater of (1) $135 multiplied by the State population, or (2) $410,520,000. 
.22 Loan Limits on Agricultural Bonds. For calendar year 2027, the loan limit amount 
on agricultural bonds under § 147(c)(2)(A) for first-time farmers is $704,800.
 .23 General Arbitrage Rebate Rules. For bond years ending in 2027, the amount of 
the computation credit determined under § 1.148-3(d)(4) of the Income Tax Regulations 
is $2,240. 
.24 Safe Harbor Rules for Broker Commissions on Guaranteed Investment Contracts 
or Investments Purchased for a Yield Restricted Defeasance Escrow. For calendar year 
2027, under § 1.148-5(e)(2)(iii)(B)(1) of the Income Tax Regulations, a broker's 
commission or similar fee for the acquisition of a guaranteed investment contract or 
investments purchased for a yield restricted defeasance escrow is reasonable if (1) the 
amount of the fee that the issuer treats as a qualified administrative cost does not 
exceed the lesser of (A) $53,000, and (B) 0.2 percent of the computational base (as 
defined in § 1.148-5(e)(2)(iii)(B)(2)) or, if more, $5,000; and (2) for any issue, the issuer 
 
 
does not treat more than $149,000 in brokers' commissions or similar fees as qualified 
administrative costs for all guaranteed investment contracts and investments for yield 
restricted defeasance escrows purchased with gross proceeds of the issue. 
.25 Gross Income Limitation for a Qualifying Relative. For taxable years beginning in 
2027, the exemption amount referred to in § 152(d)(1)(B) is $5,500.  
.26 Election to Expense Certain Depreciable Assets. For taxable years beginning in 
2027, under § 179(b)(1), the aggregate cost of any § 179 property that a taxpayer elects 
to treat as an expense cannot exceed $2,640,000 and, under § 179(b)(5)(A), the cost of 
any sport utility vehicle that may be taken into account under § 179 cannot exceed 
$33,100. Under § 179(b)(2), the $2,640,000 limitation under § 179(b)(1) is reduced (but 
not below zero) by the amount by which the cost of § 179 property placed in service 
during the 2027 taxable year exceeds $4,230,000. 
.27 Energy Efficient Commercial Buildings Deduction. For taxable years beginning in 
2027, the applicable dollar value used to determine the maximum allowance of the 
deduction under § 179D(b)(2) is $0.61 increased (but not above $1.23) by $0.02 for 
each percentage point by which the total annual energy and power costs for the 
buildings are certified to be reduced by a percentage greater than 25 percent. For 
taxable years beginning in 2027, the applicable dollar value used to determine the 
increased deduction amount for certain property under § 179D(b)(3) is $3.07 increased 
(but not above $6.13) by $0.12 for each percentage point by which the total annual 
energy and power costs for the building are certified to be reduced by a percentage 
greater than 25 percent. 
.28 Qualified Business Income. 
 
 
 
 
 
 (1) Threshold Amounts. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the threshold 
amounts under § 199A(e)(2) and phase-in range amounts under § 199A(b)(3)(B) and 
§ 199A(d)(3)(A) are:

 (2) Minimum Deduction and Qualified Business Income Amounts. For taxable 
years beginning in 2027, the minimum amount of aggerate qualified business income 
necessary for a taxpayer to be an "applicable taxpayer" under § 199A(i)(2)(A) is $1,030. 
For taxable years beginning in 2027, an applicable taxpayer’s minimum deduction 
amount provided in § 199A(i)(1)(B) for active qualified business income is $415.  
.29 Eligible Long-Term Care Premiums. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the 
limitations under § 213(d)(10), regarding eligible long-term care premiums includible in

More than 70 $6,290 
 
 
 .30 Medical Savings Accounts. 
(1) Self-only coverage. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the term "high 
deductible health plan" as defined in § 220(c)(2)(A) means, for self-only coverage, a 
health plan that has an annual deductible that is not less than $3,000 and not more than 
$4,550, and under which the annual out-of-pocket expenses required to be paid (other 
than for premiums) for covered benefits do not exceed $6,050. 
(2) Family coverage. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the term "high 
deductible health plan" means, for family coverage, a health plan that has an annual 
deductible that is not less than $6,050 and not more than $9,050, and under which the 
annual out-of-pocket expenses required to be paid (other than for premiums) for 
covered benefits do not exceed $11,050. 
.31 Interest on Education Loans. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the $2,500 
maximum deduction for interest paid on qualified education loans under § 221 begins to 
phase out under § 221(b)(2)(B), as adjusted for inflation, for taxpayers with modified 
adjusted gross income in excess of $90,000 ($180,000 for joint returns), and is 
completely phased out for taxpayers with modified adjusted gross income of $105,000 
or more ($210,000 or more for joint returns). 
.32 Limitation on Use of Cash Method of Accounting. For taxable years beginning in 
2027, a corporation or partnership meets the gross receipts test of § 448(c) for any 
taxable year if the average annual gross receipts of such entity for the 3-taxable-year 
period ending with the taxable year which precedes such taxable year does not exceed 
$33,000,000. 
 
 
 .33 Limitation on Excess Business Loss. For taxable years beginning in 2027, in 
determining a taxpayer's excess business loss, the amount under § 461(l)(3)(A)(ii)(II) is 
$264,000 ($528,000 for joint returns). 
.34 Treatment of Dues Paid to Agricultural or Horticultural Organizations. For taxable 
years beginning in 2027, the limitation under § 512(d)(1), regarding the exemption of 
annual dues required to be paid by a member to an agricultural or horticultural 
organization, is $218.44. 
.35 Insubstantial Benefit Limitations for Contributions Associated with Charitable 
Fund-Raising Campaigns. 
(1) Low cost article. For taxable years beginning in 2027, for purposes of defining 
the term "unrelated trade or business" for certain exempt organizations under 
§ 513(h)(2), "low cost articles" are articles costing $14.33 or less. 
(2) Other insubstantial benefits. For taxable years beginning in 2027, under § 170, 
the $5, $25, and $50 guidelines in section 3 of Rev. Proc. 90-12, 1990-1 C.B. 471 (as 
amplified by Rev. Proc. 92-49, 1992-1 C.B. 987, and modified by Rev. Proc. 92-102, 
1992-2 C.B. 579), for the value of insubstantial benefits that may be received by a donor 
in return for a contribution, without causing the contribution to fail to be fully deductible, 
are $14.33, $71.65 and $143.30, respectively. 
.36 Aggregate Limitation on Contributions to ABLE Accounts. For taxable years 
beginning in 2027, $20,000 (instead of the amount under provided in section 3.46(1) of 
this revenue procedure) is included in the aggregate limitation on contributions to ABLE 
accounts under § 529A(b)(2)(B)(i). 
 
 
 
 
 
 .37 Special Rules for Credits and Deductions. For taxable years beginning in 2027, 
the amount of the deduction under § 642(b)(2)(C)(i) is $5,450.  
.38 Tax on Insurance Companies Other than Life Insurance Companies. For taxable 
years beginning in 2027, under § 831(b)(2)(A)(i) the amount of the limit on net written 
premiums or direct written premiums (whichever is greater) is $3,000,000 to elect the 
alternative tax for certain small companies under § 831(b)(1) to be taxed only on taxable 
investment income. 
.39 Expatriation to Avoid Tax. For calendar year 2027, under § 877A(g)(1)(A), unless 
an exception under § 877A(g)(1)(B) applies, an individual is a covered expatriate if the 
individual's "average annual net income tax" under § 877(a)(2)(A) for the five taxable 
years ending before the expatriation date is more than $218,000.
 .40 Tax Responsibilities of Expatriation. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the 
amount that would be includible in the gross income of a covered expatriate by reason 
of § 877A(a)(1) is reduced (but not below zero) by $940,000 pursuant to § 877A(a)(3).
 .41 Foreign Earned Income Exclusion. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the 
foreign earned income exclusion amount under § 911(b)(2)(D)(i) is $137,300.
 .42 Partial Exclusion for Gain from Certain Small Business Stock. 
(1) For taxable years beginning in 2027, the $15,000,000 amount referred to in 
§ 1202(b)(4)(B) is adjusted to $15,480,000. 
(2) For taxable years beginning in 2027, the $75,000,000 amount referred to in the 
introductory clause in § 1202(b)(4) is adjusted to $77,390,000. 
.43 Debt Instruments Arising Out of Sales or Exchanges. For calendar year 2027, a 
qualified debt instrument under § 1274A(b) has stated principal that does not exceed 
 
 
$7,704,600, and a cash method debt instrument under § 1274A(c)(2) has stated 
principal that does not exceed $5,503,300. 
.44 Basic Exclusion Amount for Estate Tax. For calendar year 2027, the basic 
exclusion amount under § 2010(c)(3) is $15,480,000. The basic exclusion amount is 
used in determining the applicable credit amount against estate tax described in section 
2010(c)(1) and the applicable credit amount against gift tax described in section 
2505(a)(1). The basic exclusion amount is also used in determining the 
generation-skipping transfer exemption amount under section 2631(c). 
.45 Limitation on Aggregate Decrease in Value of Qualified Real Property in 
Decedent's Gross Estate. For an estate of a decedent dying in calendar year 2027, if 
the executor elects to use the special use valuation method under § 2032A for qualified 
real property, the aggregate decrease in the value of qualified real property resulting 
from electing to use § 2032A for purposes of the estate tax cannot exceed $1,500,000. 
.46 Annual Exclusion for Gifts and Annual Exception for Covered Gifts and Covered 
Bequests Received from a Covered Expatriate. 
(1) For calendar year 2027, the first $20,000 of gifts to any person (other than gifts 
of future interests in property) are not included in the total amount of taxable gifts under 
§ 2503 made during that year. 
(2) For calendar year 2027, the first $201,000 (instead of the amount provided in 
paragraph (1) of this section 3.46) of gifts to a spouse who is not a citizen of the United 
States (other than gifts of future interests in property) are not included in the total 
amount of taxable gifts under §§ 2503 and 2523(i)(2) made during that year. 
 
 
 (3) The tax imposed under § 2801 on the receipt of covered gifts or covered 
bequests from a covered expatriate shall apply only to the extent that the value of 
covered gifts and covered bequests received during calendar year 2027 exceeds 
$20,000. 
.47 Tax on Arrow Shafts. For calendar year 2027, the tax imposed under 
§ 4161(b)(2)(A) on the first sale by the manufacturer, producer, or importer of any shaft 
of a type used in the manufacture of certain arrows is $0.67 per shaft. 
.48 Passenger Air Transportation Excise Tax. For calendar year 2027, the tax under 
§ 4261(b)(1) on the amount paid for each domestic segment of taxable air 
transportation is $5.50. For calendar year 2027, the tax under § 4261(c)(1) on any 
amount paid (whether within or without the United States) for any international air 
transportation, if the transportation begins or ends in the United States, generally is 
$24.10. Under § 4261(c)(3), however, a lower rate of tax applies under § 4261(c)(1) to a 
domestic segment beginning or ending in Alaska or Hawaii, and the tax applies only to 
departures. For calendar year 2027, the rate of tax is $12.10. 
.49 Tax on Certain Uses of Crude Oil and Petroleum Products. For calendar year 
2027, the tax imposed under § 4611(a) on crude oil received at a United States refinery 
and petroleum products entered into the United States for consumption, use, or 
warehousing is $0.18 per barrel, which is the sum of the inflation-adjusted Hazardous 
Substance Superfund financing rate of $0.18 per barrel under § 4611(c)(2)(A) and the 
applicable Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund financing rate of $0.00 per barrel under 
§ 4611(c)(2)(B) and (f)(2). 
 
 
 
 .50 Reporting Exception for Certain Exempt Organizations with Nondeductible 
Lobbying Expenditures. For taxable years beginning in 2027, the annual per person, 
family, or entity dues limitation to qualify for the reporting exception under § 6033(e)(3) 
(and section 5.05 of Rev. Proc. 98-19, 1998-1 C.B. 547), regarding certain exempt 
organizations with nondeductible lobbying expenditures, is $151.00 or less. 
.51 Notice of Large Gifts Received from Foreign Persons. For taxable years 
beginning in 2027, § 6039F authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury or the Secretary's 
delegate to require recipients of gifts from certain foreign persons to report these gifts if 
the aggregate value of gifts received in the taxable year exceeds $21,240.31. 
.52 Payment Reporting Threshold. For payments made in calendar year 2027, the 
reporting threshold for payments described in § 6041(a) is $2,100. 
.53 Persons Against Whom a Federal Tax Lien Is Not Valid. For calendar year 2027, 
a federal tax lien is not valid against (1) certain purchasers under § 6323(b)(4) who 
purchased personal property in a casual sale for less than $2,070, or (2) a mechanic's 
lienor under § 6323(b)(7) who repaired or improved certain residential property if the 
contract price with the owner is not more than $10,340. 
.54 Property Exempt from Levy. For calendar year 2027, the value of property 
exempt from levy under § 6334(a)(2) (fuel, provisions, furniture, and other household 
personal effects, as well as arms for personal use, livestock, and poultry) cannot exceed 
$12,370. The value of property exempt from levy under § 6334(a)(3) (books and tools 
necessary for the trade, business, or profession of the taxpayer) cannot exceed $6,180. 
 
 
 .55 Exempt Amount of Wages, Salary, or Other Income. For taxable years beginning 
in 2027, the dollar amount used to calculate the amount determined under 
§ 6334(d)(4)(B) is $5,450. 
.56 Interest on a Certain Portion of the Estate Tax Payable in Installments. For an 
estate of a decedent dying in calendar year 2027, the dollar amount used to determine 
the "2-percent portion" (for purposes of calculating interest under § 6601(j)) of the estate 
tax extended as provided in § 6166 is $2,010,000. 
.57 Failure to File Tax Return. In the case of any return required to be filed in 2028, 
the amount of the addition to tax under § 6651(a) for failure to file an income tax return 
within 60 days of the due date of such return (determined with regard to any extensions 
of time for filing) will not be less than the lesser of $555 or 100 percent of the amount 
required to be shown as tax on such return. 
.58 Failure to File Certain Information Returns, Registration Statements, etc. For 
returns required to be filed in 2028, the penalty amounts under § 6652(c) are:

 .60 Failure to File Partnership Return. In the case of any return required to be filed in 
2028, the dollar amount used to determine the amount of the penalty under § 6698(b)(1) 
is $265. 
.61 Failure to File S Corporation Return. In the case of any return required to be filed 
in 2028, the dollar amount used to determine the amount of the penalty under 
§ 6699(b)(1) is $265. 
.62 Failure to File Correct Information Returns. In the case of any failure relating to a

 .64 Failure to Comply with Information Reporting Requirements Relating to Qualified 
Opportunity Funds and Qualified Rural Opportunity Funds. In the case of any return 
required to be filed in 2028, the penalty amount under § 6726 for failure to file a return in 
the time and manner prescribed for a qualified opportunity fund or qualified rural 
opportunity fund under § 6039K is $520 per day with a maximum penalty of $10,000 per 
return ($52,000 if the gross assets of the fund are greater than $10,560,000). If the 
failure to file in the time and manner prescribed is due to intentional disregard, then the 
penalty is $2,640 per day with a maximum penalty is $52,000 per return ($264,000 if the 
gross assets of the fund are greater than $10,560,000). 
.65 Revocation or Denial of Passport in Case of Certain Tax Delinquencies. For 
calendar year 2027, a federal tax liability must be greater than $68,000 to be considered 
seriously delinquent tax debt under § 7345. 
.66 Attorney Fee Awards. For fees incurred in calendar year 2027, the attorney fee 
award limitation under § 7430(c)(1)(B)(iii) is $270 per hour. 
 
 
 .67 Periodic Payments Received Under Qualified Long-Term Care Insurance 
Contracts or Under Certain Life Insurance Contracts. For calendar year 2027, the stated 
dollar amount of the per diem limitation under § 7702B(d)(4), regarding periodic 
payments received under a qualified long-term care insurance contract or periodic 
payments received under a life insurance contract that are treated as paid by reason of 
the death of a chronically ill individual, is $445. 
.68 Qualified Small Employer Health Reimbursement Arrangement. For taxable 
years beginning in 2027, to qualify as a qualified small employer health reimbursement 
arrangement under § 9831(d), the arrangement must provide that the total amount of 
payments and reimbursements for any year cannot exceed $6,700 ($13,550 for family 
coverage). 
SECTION 4. EFFECTIVE DATE 
.01 General Rule. Except as provided in section 4.02 of this revenue procedure, this 
revenue procedure applies to taxable years beginning in 2027. 
.02 Calendar Year Rule. Section 3 of this revenue procedure applies to transactions 
or events occurring in calendar year 2027 for purposes of sections 3.07 (rehabilitation 
expenditures treated as separate new building), 3.08 (low-income housing credit), 3.14 
(transportation mainline pipeline construction industry optional expense substantiation 
rules for payments to employees under accountable plans), 3.21 (private activity bonds 
volume cap), 3.22 (loan limits on agricultural bonds), 3.23 (general arbitrage rebate 
rules), 3.24 (safe harbor rules for broker commissions on guaranteed investment 
contracts or investments purchased for a yield restricted defeasance escrow), 3.39 
(expatriation to avoid tax), 3.43 (debt instruments arising out of sales or exchanges), 
 
 
3.44 (basic exclusion amount for estate tax), 3.45 (limitation on aggregate decrease in 
value of qualified real property in decedent's gross estate), 3.46 (annual exclusion for 
gifts and annual exception for covered gifts and covered bequests received from a 
covered expatriate), 3.47 (tax on arrow shafts), 3.48 (passenger air transportation 
excise tax), 3.49 (tax on certain uses of crude oil and petroleum products), 3.53 
(persons against whom a federal tax lien is not valid), 3.54 (property exempt from levy), 
3.56 (interest on a certain portion of the estate tax payable in installments), 3.65 
(revocation or denial of passport in case of certain tax delinquencies), 3.66 (attorney fee 
awards), and 3.67 (periodic payments received under qualified long-term care insurance 
contracts or under certain life insurance contracts) of this revenue procedure. 
SECTION 5. DRAFTING INFORMATION 
     The principal author of this revenue procedure is Michael Finn of the Office of 
Associate Chief Counsel (Income Tax & Accounting). For further information regarding 
this revenue procedure, contact Mr. Finn at (202) 317-4718 (not a toll-free call).
